messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am having a problem with Rsubread in a cluster setting on a shared NFS file system (with delays, which could potentially be the problem?). After a short while, I am receiving the following message:

WARN [2018-08-02 11:26:39] cannot open file './.Rsubread_featureCounts_pid5809': No such file or directory

ERROR [2018-08-02 11:26:39] cannot open the connection

Then things crash. I am using BiocParallel to run a loop in parallel, each iteration of which calls feaureCounts from within R. in parallel.

I am really hoping this issue can be solved, I redesigned my pipeline to move from the Subread package and featureCounts to an R-only solution but now it appears I cannot use it properly :(.

Thanks,
Christian

messages.subject: featurecounts more fragments than input read pairs
messages.subject_clean: featurecounts more fragments than input read pairs
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
I have a question for the output of featurecounts (from subread package).
The total number of my input read pairs is 47168870 (reported by fastQC and STAR):

    >  Number of input reads | 47168870
    >                       Average input read length | 152
    >                                     UNIQUE READS:
    >                    Uniquely mapped reads number | 37604677
    >                         Uniquely mapped reads % | 79.72%
    >                           Average mapped length | 149.39
    >                        Number of splices: Total | 16519867
    >             Number of splices: Annotated (sjdb) | 0

But the total number of fragments reported by featurecount is 82845035, almost twice as much as the number of input read pairs. the number of SAM alignment pairs reported by htseqcount is 81037190.

    > (featurecount): Total fragments : 82845035
    >   Successfully assigned fragments : 32386307 (39.1%)

(htseqcount)

    > 81000000 SAM alignment record pairs processed. Warning: Mate pairing
    > was ambiguous for 965089 records; mate key for first such record:
    > 81037190 SAM alignment pairs processed.

This is the gff I used for count is gencode.v24.annotation.gff3

My question is that I want to know what is the definition of fragment in featurecount report? why there is more fragments compared with the input read pairs? In my understanding, each read pair indicates a fragment and the total number of fragment and total number of read pair should be equal.

Thank you for your time in advance. I asked in biostars already but thinking maybe here is more effective.

ewre

messages.subject: Re: featurecounts more fragments than input read pairs
messages.subject_clean: featurecounts more fragments than input read pairs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ewre,

featureCounts reports number of alignments. This number will be different from number of reads when more than one alignment is reported for a read. This typically happens when multi-mapping reads were reported with more than one alignment in bam/sam output. I believe this is the case for your mapping and counting.

A fragment means a read pair. It looks you count read pairs therefore featureCounts provides summary of fragment counts in its output.

Best,

Wei
